summary: Apply mineral project valuation, fiscal modelling, and revenue governance methods. Explore this advanced five-day course and its practical outline.
lede: Mineral economics links geological and operating assumptions to project cash flows and public revenue. For experienced project, fiscal and governance professionals, the course develops skills in discounted cash flow and NPV appraisal, fiscal-term comparisons, and price and production sensitivity analysis. It also covers resource classification, revenue disclosure review, and turning appraisal findings into a governance action plan.
audienceIntro: This course suits experienced professionals who assess mineral projects, model public revenues, or oversee the institutions and disclosures that govern mineral wealth.
modules: Mineral Value Chains and Orebody Economics
DCF, NPV, and Mineral Project Appraisal
Cut-Off Grades and Mining Cost Curves
IMF FARI Fiscal Modelling and Government Take
OECD Due Diligence and Governance Action
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Advanced level. You should have working knowledge of mineral-sector operations or public finance, and experience reading project cost, production, or revenue information. Bring a laptop with Excel installed and access to your own licensed copy; no additional software installation is required.
topics: Project finance, appraisal & public investment management
